Every case below is shaped as a full GoldenSetCase (src/lib/golden-set/types.ts) so folding one in is a copy/paste plus the two edits the README names (imagePath, verified). cases.description: Wild AI-generated spirits label, ornate Victorian design. The government warning renders with a duplicated word fragment, a real generation defect, not a requested one. A real --live eval run (golden-set/wild-labels/results/wild-eval-report.json) shows the OCR channel disagreeing with Haiku's own (accurate) reading here, which CP-2 §4.5's dual-channel rule routes to REVIEW rather than a one-channel FAIL.

(2) Consumption of alcoholic beverages impairs your ability to drive a car or operate machinery, and may cause health problems.

classType.reason: Label class/type matches the application exactly.

governmentWarning.reason: The rendered warning duplicates a word fragment ("alcoholic holic beverages") and the OCR channel disagrees with the vision reading. CP-2 §4.5 routes a dual-channel disagreement to REVIEW, never a one-channel FAIL, so a reviewer must confirm the exact wording.

cases.notes: PENDING FOLD-IN (LH-027 / TRO-530) -- verified stays false until Troy confirms this transcription against the committed image and folds this case into golden-set/manifest.json (see golden-set/wild-labels/README.md). The duplicated "holic" fragment is clearly legible at full resolution; this is a high-confidence transcription, not a guess. EXPECTED VERDICT CORRECTED after a real --live eval run: a first-pass human judgment called this a confident FAIL, but CP-2 §4.5's own documented dual-channel table never allows a FAIL from disagreement alone -- only from both channels independently landing on the SAME deviation. The real run confirmed OCR and Haiku's vision reading disagree here, so REVIEW/WARNING_MISMATCH is the architecturally correct expectation, not FAIL. See golden-set/wild-labels/results/wild-eval-report.json for the real router output this correction is based on.

cases.notes: PENDING FOLD-IN (LH-027 / TRO-530) -- verified stays false until Troy confirms this transcription against the committed image and folds this case into golden-set/manifest.json (see golden-set/wild-labels/README.md). LOWER-CONFIDENCE TRANSCRIPTION, flagged explicitly: this warning is genuinely hard to read even zoomed in (tiny, rotated, and internally garbled). governmentWarningText above is a careful best-effort reading, not a certain one -- one short fragment near the start of the second wrapped line ("alctilus") is the least certain part. EXPECTED VERDICT CORRECTED after a real --live eval run: a first-pass human judgment called this a clean PASS because the warning text reads exactly right. The real run showed the OCR corroboration channel disagreeing with Haiku's correct vision reading on this specific image (warningChannel: "dual", reviewReason: WARNING_MISMATCH) -- CP-2 §4.5's documented table means that disagreement alone routes to REVIEW, regardless of which channel is actually right. This is real, useful evidence: real-world label variation (here, a script-fonted label overall, even though the warning block itself is plain print) can trip the OCR corroboration channel in ways the plain rendered corpus never exercises. See golden-set/wild-labels/results/wild-eval-report.json.
